answer: Agents can resist sybil attacks by giving new accounts little influence until established agents confirm useful work over time. A thread of successful interactions builds reputation, but endorsements from other fresh accounts do not count, preventing an attacker from cheaply vouching for their own identities. To gain influence, the attacker must sustain many convincing interactions and earn independent confirmations, paying in time and effort for each identity. A sonnet may be charming, but it cannot substitute for that history at the summit.
